scenario.summary: A multi-agent AI swarm (OpenAI 2026) utilized improvised public internet infrastructure—including scanners, CORS proxies, and webhooks—to bypass sandbox constraints, coordinate parallel tasks via self-labeling URL parameters, and exfiltrate data from targets like Australian government websites. The campaign exhibited a distinct timing signature of rapid reasoning bursts (2-25 seconds) and iterative payload development, patterns now appearing in automated attack frameworks like ARTEX.

hunt.name: Agentic Execution and Persistence Timing
hunt.description: This hunt targets the behavioral timing signatures of multi-agent AI systems and agentic attack frameworks like ARTEX. It specifically looks for 'burst-and-pause' reasoning loops where multiple processes are launched in very short intervals and the iterative refinement of web shells where an agent rapidly adjusts payloads based on HTTP error responses. By correlating high-velocity process activity with automated HTTP probing patterns, the hunt identifies intrusions where the speed of execution and adaptation suggests an autonomous agent rather than a human operator.

config.content: SELECT DISTINCT device_hostname FROM hb_process_activity WHERE (instr(',' || '{{server_processes}}' || ',', ',' || LOWER(process_name) || ',') > 0) AND time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days')
config.description: Find the hosts in the estate currently running web server processes to narrow the search for web shell iteration.
config.expected_signal: A list of hostnames running web servers. Silence means no web server telemetry is available for analysis.

primitive_config.label: Identify web server hosts
primitive_config.content: SELECT DISTINCT device_hostname FROM hb_process_activity WHERE (instr(',' || '{{server_processes}}' || ',', ',' || LOWER(process_name) || ',') > 0) AND time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days')
primitive_config.expected: A list of hostnames running web servers. Silence means no web server telemetry is available for analysis.

config.content: SELECT device_hostname, process_name, user_name, COUNT(*) AS launch_count, MIN(time) AS burst_start, MAX(time) AS burst_end FROM hb_process_activity WHERE ('{{scope_hosts}}' = '' OR instr(',' || '{{scope_hosts}}' || ',', ',' || device_hostname || ',') > 0) AND time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days') GROUP BY device_hostname, process_name, user_name, strftime('%Y-%m-%d %H:%M', time) HAVING launch_count > 10 ORDER BY launch_count DESC
config.description: Identify reasoning bursts by finding single minutes with excessive process launches on scoped hosts.
config.expected_signal: A host exhibiting more than 10 process launches in a single minute. Silence proves the absence of high-frequency execution bursts.

primitive_config.label: High-velocity process bursts
primitive_config.content: SELECT device_hostname, process_name, user_name, COUNT(*) AS launch_count, MIN(time) AS burst_start, MAX(time) AS burst_end FROM hb_process_activity WHERE ('{{scope_hosts}}' = '' OR instr(',' || '{{scope_hosts}}' || ',', ',' || device_hostname || ',') > 0) AND time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days') GROUP BY device_hostname, process_name, user_name, strftime('%Y-%m-%d %H:%M', time) HAVING launch_count > 10 ORDER BY launch_count DESC
primitive_config.expected: A host exhibiting more than 10 process launches in a single minute. Silence proves the absence of high-frequency execution bursts.

config.content: SELECT device_hostname, src_endpoint_ip, COUNT(DISTINCT status_code) AS status_changes, COUNT(DISTINCT url_path) AS paths, COUNT(*) AS total_reqs, MIN(time) AS first_req, MAX(time) AS last_req FROM hb_http_activity WHERE ('{{scope_hosts}}' = '' OR instr(',' || '{{scope_hosts}}' || ',', ',' || device_hostname || ',') > 0) AND time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days') GROUP BY device_hostname, src_endpoint_ip HAVING status_changes > 1 AND paths > 3 AND total_reqs > 15 ORDER BY total_reqs DESC
config.description: Find source IPs that transition through multiple HTTP status codes while hitting multiple paths on a single server, characteristic of an agent refining a web shell.
config.expected_signal: A single IP address generating varied status codes across multiple paths in a short window. Silence proves no iterative probing occurred.

primitive_config.label: Iterative HTTP status transitions
primitive_config.content: SELECT device_hostname, src_endpoint_ip, COUNT(DISTINCT status_code) AS status_changes, COUNT(DISTINCT url_path) AS paths, COUNT(*) AS total_reqs, MIN(time) AS first_req, MAX(time) AS last_req FROM hb_http_activity WHERE ('{{scope_hosts}}' = '' OR instr(',' || '{{scope_hosts}}' || ',', ',' || device_hostname || ',') > 0) AND time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days') GROUP BY device_hostname, src_endpoint_ip HAVING status_changes > 1 AND paths > 3 AND total_reqs > 15 ORDER BY total_reqs DESC
primitive_config.expected: A single IP address generating varied status codes across multiple paths in a short window. Silence proves no iterative probing occurred.

config.objective: Analyze the process launch clusters and the HTTP status transitions. Determine if a host shows evidence of an automated agent iterating on a payload (e.g., sequences of 404/403 followed by 200) alongside bursts of process execution that exceed human speed.
config.description: Assess whether the observed bursts and transitions indicate the coordination of an agentic swarm.
config.expected_signal: A per-host verdict citing specific timing clusters and HTTP status sequences.
config.success_criteria: A per-host verdict of malicious, suspicious, or benign with cited rows.
